title: How the Iran War Threatens the Global Food, Energy and Other Supplies
partialText: Beyond its effects on oil and gas, the unfolding war in the Middle East is roiling shipping and airfreight, threatening the availability of a vast range of goods.

title: Consumer Prices Rose in January, Before Iran War Added Price Pressures
partialText: Economic growth at the end of 2025 was revised downward and consumer prices rose at the start of 2026.

title: Trump Removes Sanctions on Russia to Help Oil Flow Amid Iran Conflict
partialText: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said it was “unfortunate” that the move could benefit Russia, but maintained that it was only for the short term.

title: Trump Administration Readies Plans to Dismantle NCAR Research Lab
partialText: Proposals include transferring a supercomputer to the University of Wyoming and shifting a space weather lab to a private company.

title: E.P.A. Moves to Weaken Limits on Ethylene Oxide
partialText: The gas, ethylene oxide, plays a crucial role in sterilizing medical devices. But long-term exposure is linked to several types of cancer and other ailments.

title: Wall Street Bankers Offered Lucrative Access to Join the Pentagon
partialText: A presentation from a headhunting firm aimed to recruit Wall Street investors to the Pentagon by offering “unmatched access” to government officials and fund-raising opportunities among foreign sovereigns.

title: Cuba Acknowledges Talks with Trump Officials For the First Time
partialText: President Miguel Díaz-Canel, whose country is rapidly running out of fuel, said the talks were based on “respect for the political systems of both countries.”

title: After Synagogue Attack in Michigan, Some Jews Wonder How Much More Security Is Possible
partialText: “We are synagogues — we are houses of worship,” one rabbi said. “We are not Fort Knox.”

title: What We Know About Michigan Synagogue Attack on Temple Israel
partialText: The attacker who drove into Temple Israel in West Bloomfield Township, a 41-year-old naturalized U.S. citizen, is dead. No one else was killed.

title: His Harvard Lab Was Thriving. Then Came the Cuts.
partialText: Will Mair, who studies aging, lost almost all his research funds when the White House cracked down on Harvard. He was wholly unprepared for the upheaval that followed.

title: Behind the Scenes of the 2026 Oscar Best Picture Nominees: ‘Sinners,’ ‘Hamnet’ and More
partialText: In these videos, directors walked us through pivotal sequences from their 2026 Academy Award-nominated films.

title: When a President Gets Addicted to Regime Change
partialText: Venezuela gave Trump a taste of success. This isn’t the first time an American president has gotten hooked on overthrowing foreign governments.

title: Joaquin Castro Is on a Quest to Get Detained Immigrants Released
partialText: The Texas Democrat has used his perch in Congress to highlight sympathetic cases in his push to free detainees and call attention to the consequences of President Trump’s immigration agenda.

title: Phones ‘Ringing Off the Hook’ for Ukraine Defense Firms as Mideast Seeks Help
partialText: Ukraine wants to leverage its defense expertise into security partnerships and to reap potentially vast profits for its arms industry.

title: How Recovery Scams Retarget Victims of Fraud
partialText: Many cybercrime victims are retargeted by online scammers posing as lawyers or other professionals who promise they can recover stolen money.

title: Honda Scraps Plans for E.V.s While Start-Ups Forge Ahead
partialText: The Japanese company’s retreat echoes moves by other traditional carmakers as the industry divides between electric vehicle haves and have-nots.

title: John F. Burns, Prize-winning Foreign Correspondent for The Times, Dies at 81
partialText: In a 40-year career that brought him two Pulitzers, he reported from trouble spots around the world, eloquently conveying the chaos of war.

title: Alas, You Will Never Look Like J.F.K. Jr. in Your Chinos
partialText: Recent marketing campaigns and TikToks reflect the craze for “Love Story.” They show that the Kennedy archetype still can’t be purchased.

title: The Death Penalty Is Indefensible. It’s Also on the Rise.
partialText: The surge in capital punishment is a cruel and unjust development.

title: Mussolini Would Have Loved Trump’s Ballroom
partialText: Trump’s plans for Washington bring to mind what Mussolini did — and tried to do — to Rome.

title: A Dangerous Bottleneck
partialText: Iran is turning the Strait of Hormuz into a battlefield, proving that a short and surgical war with Iran could be a fantasy.

title: How Do You Feel About Traveling Right Now? We Want to Know.
partialText: With spring and summer travel season beginning amid a war in the Middle East, a partial government shutdown and more, we’d like to hear how your travel plans are changing.

title: Pink Floyd Guitar Is Sold for a Record $14.55 Million
partialText: The black Fender Stratocaster, played by David Gilmour on six of the band’s albums including “The Dark Side of the Moon,” broke the record for the most expensive guitar sold at auction.

title: ‘A Lot of Life Years Lost’: How NAFTA Shortened American Life Spans
partialText: A study tracks how the North American Free Trade Agreement and trade competition with Mexico led to earlier deaths for American factory workers.

title: The Challenge of Helping Homeless People Who Avoid New York’s Shelters
partialText: Mayor Zohran Mamdani has been reluctant to force people indoors, even in dire weather. But conditions, whether on the streets or in shelters, can be dangerous.

title: A Visit to a Temple at the Heart of the Thailand-Cambodia Conflict
partialText: A rare visit to a Khmer temple on Thailand and Cambodia’s border showed how deadly clashes between the two countries have scarred a heritage site.
